products.name: Brebirousse d'Argental
products.tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Fromi - Rhone-Alpes, France
products.description: Mild. Creamy. Buttery. Rich. Any questions? Brebirousse d'Argental is one of those cheeses that you can't help but love. In fact, if you say you don't, one might either question your honesty, or wonder if you were describing a different cheese. Essentially it is a sheep's milk brie with a more ultra-silky texture and a mild sweetness. Add the striking orange rind and all you are lacking is a crusty loaf of bread and a glass of wine!

products.name: Fresh Ricotta
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Calabro Cheese Co. - East Haven, CT
products.description: Calabro ricotta is a special cheese. The texture is impossibly light, fluffy and creamy. Flavors are milky, buttery & sweet. Once you try it, it will be impossible to go back to the generic tubs you find at your local grocery store. The curd is still hand-dipped and hand-packed into Calabro’s instantly recognizable metal containers that are pierced with tiny holes to allow the whey to drain, even after the cheese is shipped. Delicious when enjoyed as is, it is also an essential ingredient for your ravioli, lasagna and cannoli filling. If that's not all, it is also great for baking, or drizzling with honey for an amazing dessert.

products.name: Perail de Brebis
products.tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Fromagerie a Millau/Papillon - Aveyron, France - 3.5oz
products.description: Made in Aveyron in the Midi-Pyrenees region of southern France, Perail de Brebis is a soft ripened sheep's milk cheese with a thin and velvety rind and a dense, creamy texture. It has faint aromas of hay and earth, but is mild and sweet enough to appeal to a wide audience. When allowed to reach room temperature, it will become extremely soft and runny - perfect for spooning onto a crusty loaf of bread. Enjoy with a crisp white or rosé from southern France.

products.name: Primo Pascolo
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Caseificio Rabbia - Piedmont, Italy
products.description:
Primo Pascolo, which translates to “first pasture,” is an ode to Spring in Piedmont. The cheese’s lively aromatics capture the succulent smells of a spring meadow. This raw cow’s milk, natural rind cheese is delicately tangy and vegetal, finishing with subtle yet complex hints of buttered popcorn and clover honey. The cheese’s signature springy texture is divinely doughy and fun to eat. Primo Pascolo is great all on its own as a table cheese for snacking but is also an amazing ingredient melted into risotto or creamy pasta to kick up the umami.

Caseificio Rabbia is dedicated to preserving the local traditional cheeses that are integral ingredients in the Piedmontese cuisine. They are located in Raffia near Cuneo - at the foothills of the Alps where they also have a special maturation cave that provides the perfect environment to capture the unique microbial character of the region. These flora in turn, populate on the cheese’s natural rinds, and ultimately aid in cultivating the resulting flavors in the finished cheese. These understated flavors are expressive of the native environment and lend a depth and unique character to this otherwise deceptively subtle class of cheeses. Currently in their 5th generation, the Rabbia family is dedicated to producing raw milk cheese, made from local herds within 1 kilometer of their facility. The resulting tomas are soothing, subtle and extremely snackable.

products.name: Brie de Jouvence
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Ferme de la Tremblaye - Ile-de-France, France
products.description: Brie de Jouvence is the closest thing to traditional raw milk French brie. Low temperature pasteurization, the highest quality milk, and traditional Norman methods of production result in a flavor profile that is akin to the original - full flavored, creamy, grassy, lactic, and rich.

products.name: Camembert
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Le Pommier/Mons Fromagerie - Normandy, France - 9oz
products.description: This is the closest thing to traditional French camembert that you'll find in the US. Ripened by master affineur Herve Mons, the paste is deeply golden, supple and yielding. Flavors are earthy and buttery with pleasant aromas of mushroom and truffle. Enjoy at room temperature with a crusty baguette, slice and serve atop a fresh salad, or sprinkle with chopped garlic and fresh herbs and bake until warm and molten.

products.name: Carboncino
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow, Goat & Sheep - Caseificio dell'Alta Langa - Piedmont - 5oz
products.description: This lovely Italian cheese hails from the agricultural heart of Piemonte. The name comes from the dusting of charcoal gray ash that covers the soft, silky white interior. Made from a blend of cow, goat, and sheep milk, each of which adds delicate nuances of flavor to the cheese. The texture is light and spongy.

products.name: Delice de Bourgogne
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Lincet - Burgundy, France
products.description: From the Burgundy region in France, Delice de Bourgogne is made with cow's milk that has been enriched with crème fraiche. The result is a decadent, full-flavored, but mellow cheese with a smooth, melt-in-the-mouth texture. It has a wonderful mushroomy aroma, with a pleasantly tangy finish. Nearly impossible to resist, it pairs perfectly with Champagne and fresh berries.

products.name: Fromage d'Affinois
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Guilloteau - Rhône-Alps, France
products.description: Don't know what kind of cheese your guests like? Choose Fromage d'Affinois. This soft-ripened double crème is lush, decadent and silky. With just a faint aroma of mushrooms on the rind, the mild & buttery flavors will please the crowd without being boring.

products.name: Moses Sleeper
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Jasper Hill Creamery - Greensboro, VT
products.description: Moses Sleeper is made with pasteurized cow's milk by Jasper Hill Farm in Vermont. Named after a historic local pioneer scout, this cheese is akin to a more mild version of Reblochon. The flavor is approachable and savory with hints of fresh milk, hay, toasted nuts and butter. Beneath the thin, bloomy rind, the interior paste is ivory white in color with a semi-soft, gooey texture. Pairs well with a crisp apple, cured meats, and a crusty baguette.

products.name: Bocconcino di Langa
products.tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Caseificio della'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy - 4oz
products.description: Meaning "little mouthful," Bocconcino is made with goat's milk that has been enriched with cream. It has a thin, soft, edible rind and a smooth ivory paste. Flavors include notes of tangy, fresh cream and subtle hints of grass. Enjoy with crusty bread at room temperature.

products.name: St. Stephen, 8oz
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Four Fat Fowl - Stephentown, NY
products.description: Four Fat Fowl is the cheesemaking project dreamed up by a self-proclaimed family of maniacal cheese lovers. Their commitment to making locally-sourced, handcrafted cheeses began when they turned their Sunday dinner table discussions into reality in 2013. Through careful crafting, they make cheeses that showcase the bounty of the Hudson Valley and please palates far and wide. It seemed only fitting that their name should be locally-sourced as well. Stephentown, NY has a rich history going back to the colonial era. In the seventeenth century, the Dutch colonized the Hudson Valley and established a system of landholding called patroonship. The patroon acted as the landlord to tenants who rented land to live on and farm. Stephentown was named after Stephen Van Rensselaer, the last patroon of the patroonship that now comprises Rensselaer County. His tenants called him the “Good Patroon” because he was lenient in collecting rent, which included a day’s labor, ten to twenty bushels of wheat per hundred acres, and “four fat fowl.” St. Stephen, their award-winning flagship cheese, is a handcrafted triple cream that bursts with buttery and milky overtones. This cheese boasts a smooth, silky interior made from fresh, all natural jersey cow milk and cream. A bloomy rind adds an earthy flavor with nutty undertones. St. Stephen will leave you wanting more to share with a friend and a glass of bubbly!

products.name: Tentation de Saint-Felicien, 6oz
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - La Fromagerie l'Etoile - Rhone-Alps, France
products.description: Produced in the Rhône-Alpes by La Fromagerie l’Etoile, makers of St Marcellin and St Felicien, Tentation came about as a way to use surplus cream, by adding it to the milk before making the cheese. Once ripe, the cheese becomes soft and gloriously runny. Delightfully rich and creamy, it is almost obligatory that Tentation be scooped up with a crusty baguette.

products.name: Drunk Monk
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Johan Deweer - Belgium
products.description: Third-generation Belgian cheesemaker Johan Deweer was born into a farming and dairy family. He spent his childhood absorbing everything he could along the way, immersing himself in the family business, which included both raising livestock and growing crops. What makes this cheese special is the producer’s partnership with Kaasaffineurs Van Tricht to use a special beer wash for the ripening rind, Rex, a Belgian blonde ale with Cascade hops created by Van Tricht and organic Belgian brewer, Brouwerij Anders. The resulting Trappist monk-style cheese is made from pasteurized milk from Holstein and Brown Swiss cows and vegetarian rennet. Aged for five to seven weeks, it is semisoft, silky, and sweet like freshly churned butter or heavy cream. It has brioche-like yeasty notes from the Belgian blonde ale wash, a sweet creaminess, and a fudgy, gooey, and pliable texture. Great with everything from a cheese board to burgers to fondue!

products.name: Brillat Savarin
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Delin - France
products.description: Named for the French gastronome Brillat Savarin who famously said "tell me what you eat and I'll tell you what you are." Well...if you eat this cheese, suffice to say you are really awesome. A triple creme, meaning it has a minimum of 75% butterfat, Brillat Savarin is as decadent as cheeses come. Rich? Yes. Heavy? Nope. Impossibly smooth and creamy, it is enrobed with a pillowy soft, edible cotton rind. The cheese literally cries out for Champagne! Bubbles required!

products.name: Belgioso Burrata
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - BelGioioso - Green Bay, WI - 8oz
products.description: Traditionally from Puglia in southern Italy, this is one of the freshest of all cow's milk cheeses. Milky, sweet, fresh mozzarella on the outside, with molten ribbons of curd and cream on the inside. Each 8oz package contains two 4oz pieces of burrata packed in water for optimum storage. Drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of sea salt and serve with crusty bread. You can work up from there by adding any of the following: grilled bread, prosciutto, salame, sliced tomatoes, fresh herbs, grilled vegetables, aged balsamic or sauteed rapini.

products.name: Buf Buffalo Burrata
products.tagline: Pasteurized Buffalo - Buf Creamery - El Rosal, Columbia - 8oz
products.description: Imported from the Columbia...yes, that's right, Columbia. Trust us, if it wasn't really good, we wouldn't be selling it. You love burrata, we know this. You also love mozzarella di bufula. Well, time for these two to meet. Buf's Burrata di Bufula combines two great things - the bright, tangy of buffalo milk and the molten texture of fresh burrata. Each package contains one, 8oz piece of fresh burrata di bufala packed in water for optimum storage.

products.name: Buf Mozzarella di Bufala
products.tagline: Pasteurized Buffalo - Buf - El Rosal, Columbia - 8oz
products.description: Imported from the Columbia...yes, that's right, Columbia. Trust us, if it wasn't really good, we wouldn't be selling it. Mozzarella di Bufala is wonderfully fresh and delicate with a pleasant tang. This is the perfect cheese to use on your Pizza Margherita, in a salad or with other classic Italian recipes. Each package contains one, 8oz piece of fresh mozzarella packed in water for optimum storage. Voted the #1 Mozzarella in 2016 by the American Cheese Society.

products.name: Epoisses
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Berthaut - Burgundy, France
products.description: After having been almost completely out of production during both World Wars, Epoisses was resurrected in the 1950s. The signature rind is washed with brine and Marc de Bourgogne (the local pomace brandy) and can range in color from light orange to nearly brick red. It has an intense and pungent aroma, with more subtle flavors of bacon and custard. No need for cheese knives or a cutting board - just spoon the creamy paste onto a crusty French baguette and enjoy with any wine from Burgundy.

products.name: Florette
products.tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Fromagerie Guilloteau - Rhone-Alps, France
products.description: Love brie but in the mood for something a bit less barnyard and a bit more bright? Look no further. Florette combines the creamy, lush texture of it's cow's milk cousin with the bright piquancy of goat cheese. Ivory white in color with a ultra-creamy, spreadable texture, this cheese is a perfect gateway goat.

products.name: Fresh Mozzarella
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Grande Cheese Co. - Brownsville, WI
products.description: Originally made using water buffalo's milk, the cow's milk version is perfect for your Caprese Salad or Pizza Margherita. Slice into medallions and drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of sea salt for a simple, but satisfying appetizer. Four rounds to a pound, each piece is packed in a little water for freshness. Feel free to add a little tap water for storage. Before using it on pizza, drain the water and let the cheese rest in the fridge for an hour. Pour off excess water (this would have wound up in the middle of your pizza), use and enjoy!

products.name: Gina Marie Cream Cheese
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Sierra Nevada Cheese Co. - Willows, CA
products.description: Gina Marie is the original natural cream cheese. With all due respect to the mass produced cream cheese that you find at your local grocery store, there really is no comparison. Made using only milk, cream, and salt, this cheese is void of any fillers, stabilizers, and gums. Light and fluffy in texture, fresh and creamy in flavor, use it liberally whenever you have a craving for cream cheese.

products.name: Harbison Mini
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Jasper Hill Farm - Greensboro, VT
products.description: Harbison is named for Anne Harbison, affectionately known as the grandmother of Greensboro, VT. Harbison is a soft-ripened cheese with a rustic, bloomy rind, made by Jasper Hill Farm. Young cheeses are wrapped in strips of spruce cambium, the tree's inner bark layer, harvested from the farm's woodlands. Harbison is woodsy and sweet, balanced with lemon, mustard, and vegetal flavors. Before enjoying, be sure to bring it up to room temperature - then you can spoon the interior paste onto a crusty baguette!

products.name: L'Affine au Chablis, 200g
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - La Formagerie Germain - Burgundy, France
products.description: A true regional speciality, l'Affiné au Chablis Germain cheese is made from pasteurized cow's milk. Its lightly gold-tinged rind reveals a meltingly soft and creamy center. It gets its distinct flavor and characteristic color from its wash with Chablis wine. It has a lush, creamy texture with flavors that are mild with a fresh, floral and fruity aroma.

products.name: La Tur
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow, Goat & Sheep - Caseificio dell'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy - 8oz
products.description: Made by Caseificio dell'Alta Langa near the town of Alba in northern Italy, La Tur is a dense and creamy blend of cow, sheep, and goat's milk. The rind is soft, wrinkled, thin and delicate. The interior paste is ivory in color with a light, fluffy, mousse-like texture, becoming extremely soft and creamy under the rind. Flavors are rich and sweet with a subtle tang. Due to its fragility, it is encased in a cupcake-like wrapper and placed in a protective plastic container. When ripe, the molten creamline commonly sticks to the paper as it is removed. The cheese that ends up on the paper will taste as good as the cheese that ends up on your cheeseboard!

products.name: Langres
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Germain - Champagne-Ardenne, France
products.description: Langres is a French cow's milk cheese that originated from the plateau of Langres in the region of the Champagne Ardenne. Successive washings during aging result in a beautiful orange hue and a pungent, intense aroma. The flavor, however, is much more mellow and approachable. Combine these characteristics with a super dense, creamy texture and a glass of Champagne and you will be very happy.

products.name: Le Secret des Lys
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Jean Perrin - Franche Comte, France
products.description: Remember St. Marcellin? We do too. Due to forces beyond our control, it's not available to us anymore. Queue Secret des Lys. It has all the same qualities - rich, molten, spoonable & a free crock! The more you buy, the more ramikens you will have for olives & pits, too! Let it come to room temperature, or even gently heat it in the oven before serving! Instant fondue!

products.name: Mt. Tam, 7oz
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Cowgirl Creamery - Petaluma, CA - 8oz
products.description: Named after the 4,000 ft. Mt Tamalpais that lies at the southern end of Marin County, Mt. Tam is a triple cream cheese made using local organic milk with the addition of cream. This bloomy rind cheese is silky smooth, creamy and extremely rich. Buttery and mellow with a faint aroma of mushrooms, it has wide appeal without a shortage of character.

products.name: Nocciolo
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow/Goat/Sheep - Caseificio dell'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy
products.description: Il Nocciola, meaning hazelnut in Italian, is a beautiful cow/goat/sheep combo from Northern Italy's Piedmont region. It is sweet, buttery, bright & impossibly creamy. Despite it's diminutive stature, it brings maximum impact. It's hard to find anyone who doesn't love this cheese, especially when you hand them a glass of bubbly to go with it!

products.name: Saint-Nectaire Laitier AOP
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Xavier David - Auvergne, France
products.description: Saint-Nectaire has been made in the Auvergne region of France since at least the 17th century. This cheese is aged traditionally on rye straw for at least 4 weeks in damp volcanic cellars in the town of Allanche. Affineurs wash the cheese with a salt water brine during maturation and turn the cheese over on a regular basis to achieve its characteristic orange and grey rind. Known for its creamy, unctuous paste and hazelnut flavor, Saint-Nectaire pairs easily with charcuterie and a crusty baguette and melts beautifully into recipes!

products.name: Sawtooth
products.tagline: Row Cow - Cascadia Creamery - Trout Lake, WA
products.description: Made by the Cascadia Creamery in Trout Lake, WA. Named for the nearby Sawtooth Huckleberry Fields on the shoulder of Mt. Adams where Native Americans have picked berries for thousands of years. This semi-soft, washed rind cheese has a fudgy, smooth texture and a complex, peaty flavor with notes of freshly pickled walnuts and honeycomb.

products.name: Taleggio
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Delitia - Lombardy, Italy
products.description: Taleggio is a cheese whose origin dates back to the 10th century. Production takes place in the Val Taleggio region of northern Italy, from which its name is derived. Its pungent, washed-rind aroma belies its more mild, buttery and mushroomy flavor. The texture is creamy, rich and spreadable, becoming increasingly softer as the cheese ages. Taleggio's creamy texture makes it perfect to fold into risotto, pasta and sauces, but there is perhaps no better way to enjoy it than with the end of a fresh baguette.

products.name: Vacherousse d'Argental
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromi - Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes, France
products.description: Vacherousse d'Argental is a soft cow's milk cheese. The cheese is washed with annatto to create its distinctive orange-red color and then aged for two weeks to allow its white mold rind to develop. This decadent double creme cheese is buttery and delicate. Serve with crusty bread and slices of crisp apple. Sure to be a crowd pleaser!
